Name: Dream A Little Dream - A Small Event Expansion
Author: CozyPsychologist
Description:
[center][size=5][u][b]Dream A Little Dream[/b][/u][/size][/center]
[center][/center]
[size=4]Dream A Little Dream[/size][size=4] is a narrative dream mod for Stardew Valley that follows the farmer through a series of strange, folkloric dreams tied to the valley, its spirits, and the memory of their grandfather.[/size]
[size=4]
As the seasons pass, the farmer begins experiencing dreams centered around mysterious animals: a sleeping fox beneath the moon, a white owl carrying something forgotten, a stag whose antlers hold stars, a rabbit waiting beneath the snow, and others.[/size]
[size=4]
Each dream tells a small story of its own. Some are comforting. Some are unsettling. Some offer advice that only makes sense after waking.[/size]
[size=4]
The dreams are connected by an unknown figure who signs their letters simply:[b] [/b]The Dreamer[/size]
[size=4]
After every dream, a letter arrives containing a painting of what the farmer saw that night. There are eleven paintings to collect.[/size]
[size=4]
The first ten dreams slowly explore themes of memory, grief, uncertainty, patience, fear, hope, regret, and the strange ways people find their way forward. The eleventh and final dream is different.[/size]
[size=4]
On the 28th after the tenth dream has been seen, The Dreamer finally reveals himself and explains why the spirits of the valley have been visiting the farmer's sleep. Long ago, the farmer's grandfather spoke highly of the grandchild who would one day inherit his farm. The spirits wanted to know whether his faith had been deserved.[/size]
[size=4]
The dreams were their way of finding out.[/size]
[size=4]
The final painting is a portrait of The Dreamer himself. But finishing the dreams does not mean he disappears.[/size]
[size=4]
After receiving the final painting and letter, The Dreamer can be found in the Town cemetery every Saturday night from 8:00 PM until 2:00 AM.[/size]
[size=4]
Talking with him draws from a large pool of post-dream dialogue. He may offer strange advice, complain about other spirits, mention dreams the farmer does not remember having, make unsettling observations about the valley, or become distracted by something that apparently is not visible to anyone else.[/size]
[size=4]
Some visits become full conversations, allowing the farmer to respond to him directly. You can ask about the spirits, your grandfather, the dreams, death, memory, or The Dreamer himself. Other conversations are considerably less useful.[/size]
[size=4]
He may ask whether your shadow has been behaving normally.[/size]
[size=4]
He may inform you that your farmhouse snores.[/size]
[size=4]
He may accuse one of your scarecrows of trying to acquire a name.[/size]
[size=4]
He may ask what happens to a dream after everyone has forgotten it.[/size]
[size=4]
Dream A Little Dream is intended to feel like discovering a small piece of forgotten valley folklore: mysterious without being incomprehensible, emotional without becoming overly serious, and strange enough that visiting The Dreamer on a rainy Saturday night may become its own little ritual.[/size]
[heading]Features[/heading]
[size=4]Eleven sequential dream events with original folklore-inspired stories, eleven collectible paintings, letters from The Dreamer after each dream, a final story sequence involving the farmer's grandfather and the valley spirits, a recurring post-story Dreamer NPC, a large pool of mysterious and humorous dialogue, branching conversations with player response choices.[/size]

[size=4][b][u]FAQ[/u][/b][/size]
[size=4]Q: When do the dreams occur?[/size]
[size=4]A: On the 7th and 21st of each season. This can be toggled to random if you wish. [/size]

[size=4]Q: Can I install this mid-save?[/size]
[size=4]A: Yes, the dreams trigger on the 7th and 21st of each season.[/size]

[size=4]Q: Is it compatible with SVE?[/size]
[size=4]A: Yes[/size]

[size=4]Q: Did you use AI?[/size]
[size=4]A: No. Everything is made by me. [/size]

[size=4]Q:You know what would be cool?[/size]
[size=4]A: No, tell me. Maybe I can add it to the mod. [/size]
